title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X is a compact connected Riemann surface. (D_i)_{i∈I} is a finite non-empty family of disjoint closed conformal disks in X, presumably with centres a_i. X* is the bordered surface X minus the open disks. By uniformization, X* carries a canonical constant-curvature metric, which can be normalized to total area 1. In the hyperbolic case (excluding g=0, ν=card I ∈ {1,2}) the boundary circles ∂D_i are geodesics. Arc length then gives each boundary circle a canonical 'structure torique', i.e. a structure of torsor under R/Z: a parametrization up to rotation. The disk D_i, with its centre a_i, gives a second toric structure on ∂D_i through the rotations of the disk about a_i.

This page. Grothendieck imposes the condition that the two toric structures coincide on every ∂D_i. Then X is recovered from X* alone by 'bouchage de trous par des disques canoniques': each boundary circle with its R/Z-torsor structure is glued to a standard unit disk by a torsor isomorphism. This is canonical, because the residual rotation extends to the disk. Disk systems arising this way are called 'admissible'.

Question 8 asks how admissibility shows up in the intrinsic geometry of X. For X ≠ P^1 (genus ≥ 1), X has its canonical Bergman metric, built from holomorphic differentials. He asks how admissibility relates to the D_i being geodesic balls {x : dist_geod(x,a_i) ≤ r_i}.

He then starts the moduli version. Fix a reference closed oriented topological surface X_0 of type (g,ν); the margin restricts to hyperbolic types. The next page introduces the 'Teichmüller space with boundary' TB_{g,ν}. Its real dimension is 6g−6+3ν, which he rewrites as C^{3g−3+ν}×R^ν. He then introduces the hole-plugging map TB_{g,ν} → T_{g,ν}, conjectured to be a trivial fibration (canonical projection) with fibre R^ν.

Overall, the page defines a canonical, metric-induced way to cap bordered Riemann surfaces. Capping turns marked bordered hyperbolic surfaces into punctured surfaces with extra data. This is a step in his 'surgery of conformal surfaces', meant to make cutting and gluing of the Teichmüller tower canonical.
errors: No outright error on this page. The dimension count on the following page is correct: Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates give 6g−6+2ν for interior curves plus ν boundary lengths.

Gap: the claim that admissible disk systems with given capped surface X form exactly a ν-parameter family (fibre R^ν, e.g. 'radii') is only presumed ('je présume'). It is a non-trivial existence and uniqueness statement, a conformal-welding type fixed-point problem, and is not proved here.

The Bergman metric only exists for genus ≥ 1; Grothendieck correctly excludes P^1. For genus 1 it is flat, so 'geodesic disks' are Euclidean there, while the metric on X* is hyperbolic. The comparison in Question 8 is therefore between metrics of different natures, which the note does not address.

ideas.what: Boundary circles of a bordered Riemann surface acquire a canonical R/Z-torsor ('toric') structure from arc length in the uniformizing metric with geodesic boundary.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary parametrization up to rotation induced by the hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary; cf. parametrized boundaries in Segal's CFT category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hyperbolic geometry folklore; parametrized-boundary formalism due to G. Segal (c. 1987)

ideas.what: Admissible disk systems: disks whose rotational toric structure on the boundary agrees with the metric one from X*, so X is obtained from X* by canonical capping with standard disks.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical capping/sewing of bordered surfaces with parametrized boundary (sewing in Segal/Vafa/Huang); self-consistency condition between disk coordinate and hyperbolic boundary length
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sewing formalism: Segal, Vafa, Huang (late 1980s–1990s). The specific self-consistency (admissibility) condition: unsure, apparently not in the literature

ideas.what: Question 8: characterize admissibility through intrinsic geometry, e.g. comparison with geodesic balls for the canonical Bergman metric.
ideas.modern_name: Open question relating canonical metrics (Bergman/Arakelov) to canonical local coordinates/disks at points

ideas.what: Teichmüller space of bordered surfaces TB_{g,ν} ≅ R^{6g−6+3ν}, viewed as C^{3g−3+ν}×R^ν, with a hole-plugging map to T_{g,ν} conjectured to be a trivial fibration with fibre R^ν.
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller space of surfaces with geodesic boundary and its relation to punctured Teichmüller space (boundary lengths → 0 limit; Mondello, Do, Penner's decorated Teichmüller theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fenchel–Nielsen; later Penner (decorated, 1987), Mondello and others (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower and surgery informally, but not this capping map as far as I know

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines a canonical capping procedure using the hyperbolic-metric-induced toric structure on boundary circles. This yields a notion of 'admissible' disk systems, and he asks how it relates to intrinsic geometry (Bergman geodesic disks). The question appears never to have been taken up.
missed.quote: Question 8 Comment cette condition d'admissibilité se reflète-t-elle en termes de la géométrie intrinsèque de X? ... quand X est muni d'une métrique de Bergman canonique ... 'disques géodésiques' ... dist.géod(x,a_i) ≤ r_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A canonical choice of disks or local coordinates at marked points, determined by the hyperbolic structure, would give canonical sections relevant to sewing in CFT and to the comparison between bordered and punctured moduli spaces.

missed.claim: The structure here anticipates the Segal/Vafa framework of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary and sewing via standard disks: R/Z-torsor structures on boundary circles, plus gluing standard disks along them. It adds a specific canonical (metric-induced) parametrization, around 1983–84.
missed.quote: X est déduit de X* par 'bouchage de trous par des disques canoniques' (rétablissant les structures toriques sur les comp. conn. de ∂X*)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precedence point for the parametrized-boundary formalism. It also suggests a canonical slice of the infinite-dimensional space of boundary parametrizations, related to Diff(S^1)/S^1.

missed.claim: The conjecture that the hole-plugging map from bordered Teichmüller space to punctured Teichmüller space, restricted to admissible capping, is a trivial R^ν-fibration (the canonical projection C^{3g−3+ν}×R^ν → C^{3g−3+ν}).
missed.quote: (next page) l'application TB_{g,ν} → T_{g,ν} de bouchage des trous, je présume qu'elle est fibrante ... c'est la projection canonique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete, checkable statement about a canonical conformal-welding problem. Its relation to known boundary-length fibrations (Mondello; Do's limits of bordered to cusped surfaces) is unexplored.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an original but sketchy construction: a canonical metric-induced capping with a self-consistency ('admissibility') condition, plus open questions. It prefigures parametrized-boundary sewing formalisms and seems absent from the literature. However, it is not developed, and its main claims are conjectural.
transcription_corrections: 'rétablissant[?] les structures conformes[?]' should read 'rétablissant les structures toriques sur les comp. conn. de ∂X*'; the word looks like 'toriques', consistent with the previous page.
The sentence after the strike-out reads roughly 'Disons alors que les systèmes de disques (D_i)_{i∈I} dans X obtenus de la sorte sont "admissibles"'.
The margin probably reads 'i.e. variété hyperbolique (g,ν) ≠ (0,1),(0,2)', excluding the non-hyperbolic types as on the previous page.
